The name is also used in the Bible for Saint Blanca, a martyr who was tortured and executed for her faith. The name Blanca carries the meaning “White, pure, simple” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Spanish. Parents who choose Blanca usually hope their child will grow to embody white, pure, simple and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Blanca of Castile, also known as Blanca of Navarre, was the eldest daughter of King Sancho the Wise of Navarre and his wife, Blanca of Aragon. She was born around 1171 and married Alfonso VIII of Castile in 1197. Their marriage was significant because it sealed a peace treaty between the two kingdoms which had been at war. This alliance proved crucial during the Reconquista, as the combined forces of Castile and Navarre were able to successfully take the important cities of Cuenca and Calatayud from the Muslims.
historical_references.context: Peace treaty and military alliance between Castile and Navarre during the Reconquista

historical_references.reference: Blanca of Bologna, also known as the 'Blessed Blanca of Bologna', was a laywoman and mystic who lived in the 13th century. She was born around 1252 in Bologna, Italy, and was known for her extreme asceticism and devotion to the Blessed Virgin Mary. She was beatified in 1737 by Pope Clement XII.
